result.title: Seeing Is Not Planning: Spatiotemporal Planning and Plan Repair in Multimodal LLMs
result.summary: Planning in a visual world means reading the layout, foreseeing how the state will change, and following the task rules all at once. When a plan fails, a model should also use what went wrong to fix it. We call these two abilities spatiotemporal planning and plan repair, and test them with Railbound-Bench. A model sees a railway puzzle, adds tracks under a budget, and submits one complete layout; a simulator then moves all cars at once and decides whether the layout works. After a failure, the model sees what happened and may submit a new layout, up to five attempts in total. On the 200-puzzle main set, the best of nine models solves 59.5% within five attempts, the next 39.5%, and the other seven at most 10.0%; a 1,000-puzzle extended set with a wider range of difficulty is far easier, at 90.9% for the best model. Controlled studies on 180 fixed puzzles show that knowing the task is not the same as using it. GPT-6.1 Terra copies 97.2% of boards exactly and, given a correct layout as text, predicts all four requested future states in 91.3% of cases, yet only 22.8% of its first layouts work. Planning fails more often as the cars' routes interact, even among puzzles that a search solver finds equally easy. Visual feedback removes the reported fault in 175 of 417 first revisions, but only 43 of these revisions solve the puzzle, and at an equal budget of 40k tokens it does no better than fresh retries. The code and data are open-sourced on GitHub at https://github.com/liaoyanqing666/Railbound_Bench.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Railbound-Bench：模型观察铁路谜题布局，在预算内铺设轨道并提交完整方案，由模拟器统一运行判定，失败后可看结果重试最多五次；主集 200 题仅少数模型能解，另有 180 题控制实验考察「知道任务规则」与「实际使用规则」的差距。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作以失败反馈修复与等 token 预算重试作对照，发现视觉反馈修正的故障未必带来可解方案，可为 LVR 中视觉证据是否被真正使用、重试与停止决策的成本收益，以及「信息在但未被利用」的旁路问题提供核查基准。
